versions.summary: Layout corrected from Google Earth. Wooden fence, back alley, neighboring buildings and the billboard added.

Building and neighbors reshaped from Google Earth and the videos. Kitchen double door, hidden service corridor and restroom route placed as Robert describes. Existing landscaping added. Billboard removed.
Tables and chairs restyled like Bacari's LA patios: walnut tables on black iron bases, rattan bistro chairs, navy banquettes with bright pillows, rattan-back bar stools.
Rattan bistro bar stools with footrests and hoop backs, 12 more two-tops with clear staff aisles, and the two brown-topped trees made green.
Straight backs on all chairs and bar stools, and a glass double door on the upper floor opening onto the deck.
Front gate on W 6th drawn partly open so it reads as a door, and banquette back cushions in Bacari LA style bright prints over grey-striped seats.
Decks and their stairs drawn as real wood boards with wood fascia edges, and a more ornate street gate with lantern pillars, an iron arch and iron-and-wood leaves.
Eleven two-tops turned into four-tops across the decks, front terrace and garden, keeping clear staff aisles.
More planters throughout: olive and boxwood planters at the deck corners and by the gate and steps, hanging troughs on the upper deck railing, and a planted trough along the W 6th retaining wall.
The planters are now big corten boxes, about 3½ ft square and 3 ft tall, each with a small tree (olive or Texas mountain laurel) and boxwood around the trunk.

The north-east corner bank becomes a terraced limestone garden with the leaning trees up-lit at night, Texas natives, a flagstone path up to a stone bench, a runnel and bubbling basin by the deck, and an open iron fence so it shows from W 6th.
The building is painted a light blue, keeping its white trim, cedar cladding and brick chimney.
Every tree on the property is now drawn as a Texas live oak (short thick trunks, long twisting limbs, broad dark-green canopies), on top of version 12's light blue building.

Bacari-style night lighting everywhere (bistro string-light canopies over every deck, rattan pendants, table candles, wall sconces, path lights), a 20 ft automated sliding gate on the back lot, and the apartments behind can be hidden.
Up-lights for the trees at night: in-grade well lights washing each big live oak and a small spike light in every planter tree, on top of version 14's night lighting.
The streets look like streets: dark asphalt with lane markings, curbs, sidewalks, crosswalks at Pressler, street lights and parked cars, on top of version 15's tree up-lights.

Streets corrected from map data and aerial imagery: W 6th one-way westbound with three lanes and north-curb parking, Pressler one-way north below W 6th, real curb cuts and driveways, and the north side of W 6th filled in.
More Bacari-style night light: candles on every table (night only), fairy lights through all the oaks, a fire pit on the front terrace, Edison pendants over the bar and iron lanterns along the walls.
The building's back doors are now glass: steel-framed glass French doors onto the upper deck, glass kitchen doors under the deck, and a frosted glass restroom door, all glowing warm at night.
The three glass doors onto the upper deck are now one big glass door: a 16 ft opening with four folding glass panels.
